clue.text: A very strong aptitude for courtesy

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud or strong
an aptitude is a natural ability

explanation.surface: Someone has a real talent for good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Affability is friendly politeness, a close synonym of courtesy.

clue.text: Accessory for the entire year

parts.note: the entire means all of it

explanation.surface: A fashion accessory meant to be worn all year round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accessory' is the legal sense, an accomplice, not a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: An accessory to a crime is a partner or helper, which is what an ally is.

clue.text: Kitty has the last word on square bottom

parts.note: a kitty is a shared pool of money, a fund
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
a T-square is a drawing tool, so square can give T

explanation.surface: A cat insists on having the final say about a dull person's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is a pool of cash, not a cat; 'square' is the T of a T-square, not a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundament is an old word for the buttocks, a person's seat.

clue.text: Prime cheese, one franc!

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
F is the abbreviation for a single franc, the old French currency

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising top-quality cheese sold for just one franc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like an adjective for the cheese; it is a verb meaning to instruct someone in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime someone is to prepare them with information, as a barrister is instructed before a case.

clue.text: Concerned with milk for tea, call out!

indicators.note: out signals the letters of these two words thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for milk to go with their tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEA and CALL together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal is the adjective for things relating to or resembling milk.

clue.text: Boom-end hurt resettlement

indicators.note: resettlement suggests the letters being moved and placed anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The end of an economic boom brings hardship from people being relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resettlement' rearranges END and HURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a deep resonant roar, the sound that thunder makes.

clue.text: Club in urban district

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of words urban district

explanation.surface: A nightclub found in a city neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'urban' and the start of 'district'.
explanation.definitionFit: A club and a band are both a group of people joined together for a purpose.

clue.text: Musketeer at hospital so upset

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map symbol for hospital; the run across at hospital spelling the start of the name is a coincidence

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word so is read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: One of the musketeers is in hospital and feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS in this down clue. Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is one of the three title swordsmen in Dumas's novel The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Carriage used to banish fellows to Tasmania, originally

parts.note: to banish someone is to deport them
fellows are men

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word Tasmania

explanation.surface: A convict ship once used to transport men to Tasmania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle; here it is the way a person holds themselves. Tasmania was a British penal colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage and deportment both mean bearing or posture.

clue.text: Pots for bears?

definitions.meaning: pots are paunches or bellies, as in pot-belly
bears means tolerates, puts up with

explanation.surface: Containers made for bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Paunches are stomachs, and to stomach something is to tolerate it.

clue.text: After a breather, one put on a loincloth

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: a lung is the organ one breathes with
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: After a rest, someone wraps on a loincloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest; it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia.

clue.text: Pressing one's suit flatter with craft

parts.note: to court someone is to flatter or woo them
a craft is a boat or ship

explanation.surface: Ironing your suit flat with a skilled hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing one's suit' sounds like ironing; it means pursuing a romantic proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing a partner is pressing one's suit, an old idiom for seeking marriage.

clue.text: Country-dance competition in Tedder's Green?

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance
the field is everyone competing in a race

explanation.surface: A country dance contest held on a village green.
explanation.walkthrough: A tedder is a farm machine that turns cut grass to dry it, so its green is a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedder works in a meadow of mown grass being dried for fodder.

clue.text: Curmudgeon leaves solo call unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the bid is cut off

parts.note: misere is a bid in solo whist, undertaking to win no tricks

explanation.surface: A grumpy card player storms off without completing a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: Solo whist is a card game; its misere call is a bid to lose every trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A curmudgeon is a mean, grasping person, a stingy hoarder.

clue.text: Feature of steelmakers' furnace, clear symbol of home?

parts.note: clear means open, unobstructed
the fireside stands for the home, as in hearth and home

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a steelworks furnace homely.
explanation.definitionFit: The open-hearth process was a method of making steel in a shallow furnace.

clue.text: Succeed in persuading clergyman to get inside bucket

indicators.note: to get inside places the clergyman within the bucket

parts.note: a pail is a bucket
Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: Coaxing a vicar into climbing into a bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail upon someone is to talk them round into doing something.

clue.text: Mutiny of Caine, bad for tolerance?

indicators.note: a mutiny overturns order, so these letters revolt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film critic asks whether The Caine Mutiny is bad for patience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caine Mutiny is a novel and film; 'Mutiny of' rearranges CAINE and BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Abidance is the act of abiding, putting up with or enduring something.

clue.text: Organised miracle rescue

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rescue that was a planned miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges MIRACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or save it, as land is won back from the sea.

clue.text: States a following for Uncle Sam's relics

indicators.note: following places the letter after the first piece

parts.note: the States is the USA, so of the States is American

explanation.surface: Patriotic Americans gather a fan base for national memorabilia.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam personifies the US government.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and memorabilia of US history and culture.

clue.text: As a Frenchman, he painted more spruce

definitions.meaning: Jean-Marc ... was an 18th-century French portrait painter
spruce means smart and neat, so more spruce is smarter

explanation.surface: A French painter who dressed more smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and dapper, its comparative fits more spruce, and the name belongs to a French portraitist.

clue.text: String essential to daring jumpers?

parts.note: jumpers sound like knitwear needing string, but they are parachutists whose chute opens when they pull a cord

explanation.surface: A thread vital to knitting bold sweaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute is opened by pulling a cord, which skydivers depend on.

clue.text: Channel Islands succeeded with seabird in a tank

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird flourished in a water tank on the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British islands off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water.

clue.text: Dialect unusual in the kremlin?

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange accent heard in the seat of Russian power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DIALECT. A kremlin, lower case, is any Russian fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A kremlin is a fortified inner area of a Russian city, a fortress.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide, is a bonus scored to the batting side
over means additional, more than needed

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bye or wide is a bonus run, and anything over is surplus or additional.

clue.text: Square grain served in a moment

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so square can give T
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A plain grain dish served up quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is an instant, as in done in a trice.

clue.text: Pitiful tie-patch repair?

indicators.note: repair suggests the letters being mended into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patched-up tie looks rather sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges TIE and PATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means arousing pity, wretched.

clue.text: Old coin of gold or silver held by Lee, possibly?

indicators.note: held by places the silver within the other letters
possibly signals the name's letters arranged another way

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Confederate general, Lee, kept a gold or silver coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals rearranging the general's name, and 'held by' signals the container. The eagle was a US ten-dollar gold coin; 'gold or silver' reads as a pair but only silver gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle was a former US gold piece worth ten dollars.

clue.text: Tendency to be crooked

explanation.definitionFit: A natural inclination is one's bent, and something curved or corrupt is bent.

clue.text: One may bring about the downfall of a painter in the dark

definitions.text: One may bring about the downfall

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
taken as written
a cloud is a dark shadow or gloom

explanation.surface: Something that ruins an artist who is kept uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' means a fall of rain, not ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain-cloud brings a shower, a literal fall from above.

clue.text: Brilliance of Elgar transcription

indicators.note: a transcription is a reworking of music, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dazzling arrangement of a piece by Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar was an English composer; 'transcription' rearranges his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare is dazzling, intense brightness.

clue.text: He who wrote, reportedly, of Tom Brown's school colours

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the writer's surname is to be heard, not read

parts.note: Thomas Hughes wrote the novel Tom Brown's Schooldays

explanation.surface: The author of Tom Brown's Schooldays describes the school colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown's Schooldays is a Victorian novel set at Rugby School; its author was Thomas Hughes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hues are shades or tints, which is what colours are.

clue.text: Dante ultra-perverted with piece that corrupts?

indicators.note: perverted means twisted, so the letters of these words are distorted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The poet Dante grossly twisted by a corrupting work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' rearranges DANTE and ULTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance added that debases or contaminates something.
